question: which SAE features THIS INVERTER fails on, and whether that is predictable from SAE geometry alone. NOTE: labels come from maemm-qwen3-8b-invert-rl-v3-step600, so this measures the model's coverage, not a property of the features.

labels.success: best_act >= ex_last (reached a genuine corpus example)

findings: dec_lens_entropy is the strongest single predictor (AUC 0.184): a SHARPER decoder logit-lens distribution goes with FAILURE FOR THIS MODEL. Features whose decoder writes toward a few specific tokens are prediction commitments with nothing to describe.
rarity (AUC 0.790) and geometry (CV AUC 0.744 without rarity) are largely independent; together 0.823.
corpus_peak is flat (AUC 0.513, p=0.60) -- intrinsic activation strength does not predict expressibility.
enc_dec_cos is real but weak (AUC 0.602). Encoder/decoder divergence is a genuine effect but not the main axis.
scope_caveat: These predictors describe THIS inverter. They are not evidence that the features lack a textual preimage: hand-written sentences fire 29/30 of a sample of these same features at ~89% of corpus peak (see human_verbalization.csv). The 8B inverter was warm-started on ~1M PROBE (topic/cluster) directions, so sharp-decoder prediction-commitment features are plausibly out of distribution for it rather than intrinsically hard. Establishing an intrinsic limit would require the failure to survive across inverters trained to cover them.
